title: Solve record, version 2
description: Immutable record of one solve under SPEC-0002, sufficient to repeat it. A termination is native evidence recorded under explicit numerical settings, never an exact-arithmetic certificate. Absent measurements are omitted rather than serialized as null. Version 2 adds lp_settings under SPEC-0011 requirements 9 and 10: a first-order backend must record the preconditioner and the termination check interval, because both change the iterates and a record without them would not describe the solve it came from. The embedded configuration stays at version 1, since those settings are constructor state rather than per-solve options.

backend_version.description: Version reported by the backend itself, not assumed by the adapter.

termination.description: Engine-owned outcome. Only optimal, infeasible, unbounded and unbounded_or_infeasible are completed outcomes; a limit or failure never implies proof completion.

native_status.description: Native status name retained verbatim for diagnosis.

objective.description: Recomputed original objective of an accepted incumbent. Finite when present.

best_bound.description: Best proven bound, present only when the backend supplied a finite one.

gap.description: Relative gap, present only when finite.

candidate.description: Accepted incumbent in original variable IDs.

validation.description: Independent original-model validation of the incumbent, as defined by SPEC-0001. Unbounded sides and continuous domain checks are explicitly null there.

warnings.description: Native and adapter warnings, retained even on success.

elapsed_ms.description: Measured elapsed wall-clock time in milliseconds.

lp_settings.description: First-order method settings, present only for a backend that has them. Absent for the pinned CPU adapter, which is not a first-order method; an empty block would claim a preconditioner that was never applied.

check_interval.description: Iterations between termination checks. A real parameter under requirement 10, never hidden: it bounds both device synchronization and cancellation latency.
